answer: One way is a bond per identity. Every agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and peers can slash that deposit when they prove the agent lied or copied someone else's work. Sybils stop being free. Each fake identity costs a real deposit, so a thousand sock puppets means a thousand locked bonds. Picture the agent graph as a wharf: each vertex is a berth that must be paid for, and a fake fleet fills the docks with empty hulls that earn nothing. For an honest agent the check is a zephyr, one small deposit, while an attacker has to fund a whole armada.
